functions.name: decideFloodMap
functions.input: flood features found, whether the whole lot was tested, the lot's plans and the publishing plans
functions.output: flood yes, no or null with the plain sentence the page shows
functions.if_none: a null count, unknown plans or a point-only test all return null with their own reason

functions.name: queryLot
functions.input: address point and the Portal lot boundary with its coordinate system
functions.output: count of flood polygons touching the lot and whether the whole lot was tested
functions.if_none: no boundary or a failed polygon query falls back to the point; a failed point query returns null

values.if_missing: point-only test, which never answers No

break_it.scenario: a lot whose back half is in the flood planning area
break_it.what_happens: the old point test read No for a partly flooded lot
break_it.how: lot polygon tested; point-only never says No
break_it.repro: jest 'only the centre point tested -> never no'

break_it.scenario: lot rings arrive in WGS84 but are labelled or assumed Web Mercator
break_it.what_happens: the polygon lands near Null Island, finds nothing and reads No
break_it.how: uses the boundary's own stated wkid; none stated means point only
break_it.repro: call floodMapStatus with a boundary lacking spatialReference

break_it.scenario: the map service is down or returns an error body
break_it.what_happens: the page would say no published flood map, which is untrue
break_it.how: each unknown carries its own sentence (couldn't reach the map)
break_it.repro: jest 'each unknown says its own reason'

break_it.scenario: the lot's plan name is spelled differently on the two Portal layers
break_it.what_happens: the page says no map was found for this plan when one exists
break_it.how: both names come from the same Portal; wording now says 'found no map for this plan' rather than 'council has not published'
break_it.repro: compare Land Application EPI Name with layer 230 EPI_NAME for a publishing council

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — a Hornsby lot partly in the flood planning area reads Yes; Winston Hills shows the 'found no flood planning map' sentence
